title: Align module tagging with Redwood standard (cost-center, env, owner, data-class) + migration notes
author: Bruno Silva
description: Context: We’ve had inconsistent tags across the alpha modules (mix of environment/team/service-owner keys, and a few ad-hoc tags added during early scaffolding). This PR aligns all created AWS resources to Redwood’s IaC tagging standard so customer billing, ownership, and data classification show up consistently in Cost Explorer and downstream inventory/audit tools. Standard keys: cost-center, env, owner, data-class. What changed: (1) Added a shared tagging helper in each module that composes required tags + user-supplied tags in a predictable order and surfaces the final computed map via output computed_tags for troubleshooting. (2) Normalized key names across modules to the hyphenated form used in the Terraform module standards doc and internal FinOps exports: "cost-center", "env", "owner", "data-class". (3) Introduced optional inputs to make it easy to provide these tags without forcing every caller to construct a map manually: cost_center, env, owner, data_class (still supports var.tags as an escape hatch). (4) Added validation for data_class to reduce typos and drift (allowed: public | internal | confidential | restricted). (5) Updated READMEs and examples to show the canonical tag values, including guidance for enterprise locked-down VPCs. (6) Added migration notes (UPGRADE.md + README sections) describing how to move from the previous tag keys (environment/team/service_owner/dataclass) and what to expect in terraform plan. Migration/impact notes: This is an in-place tags-only update for resources created by these modules; it will show as many small tag diffs on VPC/subnets/route tables/endpoints/SGs, but should not force replacement. If you previously relied on the old keys for internal automation, you’ll need to update those consumers to the new hyphenated keys. We intentionally did not hard-fail applies if a required tag is missing for alpha; missing values default to "unknown" with a warning in docs. Enforcement can be added for beta once we have pilot feedback on required/optional expectations. Testing: terraform fmt/validate across modules, tflint/checkov clean, and integration apply matrix (us-west-2 + eu-central-1; single NAT + per-AZ NAT).

conversation: Irene Choi (review): Can we confirm the tag keys are exactly the hyphenated form from the module standards page? Some teams have been using underscores and it’s been messy for FinOps exports.
Bruno Silva (author): Yes — updated everywhere to hyphenated keys: cost-center/env/owner/data-class. Added a note to UPGRADE.md mapping old -> new, and updated examples accordingly.

Connor O'Donnell (review): Please add a short note about whether this is a breaking change. Even if resources won’t recreate, this will show large diffs and could surprise customers. Also, do we want to enforce presence of these tags now or later?

Bruno Silva (author): Added a Migration/impact section to the PR description + UPGRADE.md. For alpha, I kept it non-enforcing (defaults to "unknown") to avoid blocking pilots. We can add enforce_required_tags in beta if Product/Security wants.

Marcus Lin (review): Security nit: data-class values should be constrained. Also make sure we don’t encourage customers to put sensitive info in tag values (people sometimes put ticket content or names).
Bruno Silva (author): Added variable validation for data_class enum and a doc note: tag values should be non-sensitive metadata only; no customer data/secrets.
Sahana Iyer (review): CI: integration tests currently don’t assert tags; can we at least verify a single resource has the required keys so we catch regressions?
Bruno Silva (author): Added a lightweight assertion in the integration harness to check the VPC and one subnet include the four required keys.
Irene Choi (approve): Looks good after the docs + validation updates. Approving.
Connor O'Donnell (approve): Approved — thanks for the migration notes; please keep the non-enforcing stance for alpha.
Sahana Iyer (approve): Approved; CI changes look stable.
release_notes: Terraform modules now apply Redwood-standard tags (cost-center, env, owner, data-class) across all created AWS resources. Docs include migration guidance from legacy tag keys.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash merge; branch deleted.
